requirements.statement: Archivist must be a general local document-workbench rather than an EPP-only generated browser.
The EPP manual must be usable as the first serious workspace and proving corpus.
The repo should use a Vite-based frontend foundation so Dovaxis developers can later mirror parts they like.
The first architecture must support local-first use, human-reviewed recommendations, coworker local copies, and future export workflows.
Markdown bundles must remain the canonical v1 document source, with approved changes writing back through explicit review gates.
The normal reader surface must show the latest approved version of each document by default.
Archivist must preserve inspectable document history so a model or human reviewer can see what changed, when it changed, and why it changed, including changes from a year or more earlier.
Policy-content history must support transparency, rollback investigation, and before/after review rather than only storing the current document text.

Long-term document history must use a hybrid model: real Git commits for durable file snapshots and diffs, plus an Archivist audit ledger for proposal, approval, rationale, export, and review metadata linked to commit hashes.
Drafts and autosaves should remain outside committed document history until they are accepted through the review flow.
V1 should include a small bundled EPP seed workspace for development and demos while keeping the manifest design compatible with future full external workspaces.
Workspace and document filesystem operations should move behind the local service boundary before approved write, Git history, or export behavior is implemented.
Archivist v1 must target desktop-only local use; mobile layout and mobile smoke validation are not product requirements.
The standalone app must port the existing EPP manual-browser Markdown functionality rather than treating the scaffold renderer as sufficient.
The port must preserve EPP document navigation, Markdown rendering, compliance graph traversal, CFR linking, regulatory pages, source metadata, placeholders, and artifact/tool rendering behavior.

The port must preserve local chat/manual-agent behavior, including selected-text instructions, local provider status, proposals, pending review events, current-view sync, apply/reject, debug diagnostics, and local-only guardrails.
The port should preserve low-ceremony inline manual edits, autosaved drafts, and draft review while keeping manual edits separate from model proposal input.
Accepted model proposals and accepted manual draft batches should converge into the same review, Git history, and Archivist audit ledger path.
Regulatory and static reference documents must remain readable and searchable while being blocked from local editing writes.
Artifact and tool runtime renderer support should be driven by active EPP usage inventory before declaring full EPP migration complete.
Archivist must include the full EPP content corpus as a standalone workspace, not only a small representative seed subset.

The full EPP workspace import must preserve canonical Markdown content, project metadata, source references, retained app-facing extracted context, retained regulatory sources used for CFR and Survey Guidance views, and an audit ledger path. Normal import refresh must build and validate a non-app-facing staged candidate before promoting imported surfaces into the live epp-full workspace. Failed candidate import or validation must leave the existing live workspace usable and must not append a success import audit event. Normal import refresh must preserve app-owned state such as audit ledger, approved workbook sidecars, draft workbook state, and runtime data; destructive resets require a future explicit reset workflow. Successful normal import refresh must append a sanitized import event to the audit ledger and print a matching console summary without raw source paths, development-only source filenames, source-files paths, source_path values, browse targets, or download targets. Original office/catalog source files under source-files are development-only material and must be physically absent from the refreshed app-facing workspace. Development-only original source annotations under extracts/source-annotations must be absent or normalized without original source_path values. project/catalog.json must be normalized in place as app-facing metadata; no raw upstream catalog copy with development-only source file paths should be retained in Archivist v1. Original source records may remain only as non-browseable provenance stubs without original file paths or open/download targets. All app-facing project metadata must be sanitized so development-only original source paths do not leak through crosswalk, search, compliance, source metadata, or service responses. App-facing source provenance must not expose absolute local paths to the original source checkout. Import summaries and service-facing workspace summaries must use explicit count fields that distinguish provenance-only source records from retained regulatory sources, not a generic source_count. A repeatable post-import leak check must fail on disallowed original-source markers while allowing retained regulatory source data, but it must not scan canonical Markdown document bodies. A post-cleanup reference-integrity check must fail if retained app-facing metadata points to removed source annotations, removed source-files paths, removed raw source paths, or missing source records.

Appendix A must be handled as a first-class migration edge case because it combines Markdown, structured HVA workbook data, scoring, mitigation planning, review evidence, JSON import/export, and print/export behavior.
Appendix A migration must preserve the copyright guardrail against copying proprietary HVA worksheet language, examples, row order, visual layout, or comments.
Archivist must treat workbooks as a first-class artifact family rather than implementing Appendix A / HVA as a one-off component.
The workbook artifact contract must distinguish parent document text, workbook definition, workbook user-entered state, derived outputs, and print/export views.

Appendix A / HVA must validate the reusable workbook artifact family as the first implementation while preserving its HVA-specific scoring, mitigation, review evidence, JSON import/export, and print behavior.
Approved workbook state must be stored in structured sidecar JSON files linked to the parent document and workbook ID, while Markdown remains the explanatory wrapper and definition source.
The local service must expose reusable workbook discovery and sidecar state endpoints before the HVA UI prototype depends on workbook state.
The first HVA UI must write draft workbook sidecar state through the local service while keeping approved sidecar writes locked behind a future review/apply workflow.
The old EPP manual browser UI and layout must be treated as the parity baseline for the standalone Archivist app.

The full EPP browser shell must expose the imported full EPP document navigation, including Appendices and Appendix A as normal document routes, before deeper workbook UI polish is considered complete.
Archivist must preserve the old Markdown viewer, low-ceremony inline editing, autosave draft review, proposal lens, and local-only agent review behavior when porting the old browser experience.
Markdown, CFR, compliance, and artifact output must first be ported through a live compatibility renderer before high-value surfaces are promoted into polished React components.

SG-0013 must include service-backed workspace manifests, document metadata, and document payload reads rather than relying on static seed imports. Document-read responses must return browser-ready rendered compatibility output from current canonical source, with sanitized metadata, stable anchors, source/compliance orientation, and artifact placeholder/context data; raw Markdown alone is not sufficient as the primary normal-reader payload.
Archivist must render document views from canonical source at app view time; pre-rendered output is only for export, print, review snapshots, or disposable caches.
Archivist must define a provider-neutral local agent interface, with an LM Studio/OpenAI-compatible local endpoint as the first adapter rather than the permanent product contract.
One accepted model proposal or approved manual-draft batch should create one Git commit by default, with review-session batching reserved for a later workflow option if needed.
